extracted.intended_audience: NLP / Machine Learning researchers, dataset/annotation designers, and annotators working on peer-review analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Annotation and computational analysis of peer-review texts: identify which paper section(s) a review sentence comments on, which aspect it addresses, the statement's purpose and significance, and generate summaries/meta-reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (ABS)
rubrics_metrics.description: ABS (Abstract) — review statements that correspond to the paper's abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review-paper section layer identifies the section of the paper on which the review-statement is commenting. Labels are simple and obvious if one is familiar with ML papers. Annotate sentence-wise (or select text-segment) and record sentiment per label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (INT)
rubrics_metrics.description: INT (Introduction) — review statements that correspond to the paper's introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators should consider the sentence context when a single sentence is unclear in isolation. Multi-label allowed where a sentence addresses multiple sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (RWK)
rubrics_metrics.description: RWK (Related Work) — review statements about related literature or comparisons to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related Work comments often co-occur with novelty and meaningful comparisons aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (PDI)
rubrics_metrics.description: PDI (Problem Definition / Idea) — statements focusing on the problem formulation or core idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem Definition/Idea often garners comparatively positive attention; can overlap with Introduction or Overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (DAT)
rubrics_metrics.description: DAT (Data / Datasets) — statements about datasets, data description, or data quality used in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate at sentence- or phrase-level when the text refers specifically to data or dataset descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (MET)
rubrics_metrics.description: MET (Methodology) — review statements about the methods, theoretical formulation, algorithms, or technical approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology is a primary focus for reviewers and often inter-linked with Experiments and Empirical/Theoretical Soundness (EMP). Major/minor comments frequently target Methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (EXP)
rubrics_metrics.description: EXP (Experiments) — statements addressing experimental setup, protocols, reproducibility, training/evaluation details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments co-occur with Results and Analysis; questions are often targeted at EXP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (RES)
rubrics_metrics.description: RES (Results) — statements about the experimental outcomes, performance numbers, and reported findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results often receive sentiment differences between accepted and rejected reviews and relate to Impact and Novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (ANA)
rubrics_metrics.description: ANA (Analysis) — critical analysis of results, ablation studies, error analysis, or deeper interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis is less frequent than Methodology/Experiments but important for assessing empirical rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (TNF)
rubrics_metrics.description: TNF (Tables and Figures) — comments targeting the paper's tables, figures, visualizations, and their clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation and formatting concerns are often on Tables and Figures; annotate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (FWK)
rubrics_metrics.description: FWK (Future Work) — statements discussing possible extensions or future directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less prominent in reviews; annotate when reviewers explicitly mention future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (BIB)
rubrics_metrics.description: BIB (Bibliography) — comments about citations, missing references, or bibliography quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliography comments tend to be neutral and co-occur with Meaningful Comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (EXT)
rubrics_metrics.description: EXT (External Information) — statements that reference external sources or information not in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EXT when reviewers bring in outside information or context; annotate with sentence context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 — Review-paper section correspondence (OAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL (Overall paper) — generic comments about the paper as a whole rather than a specific section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall comments can appear anywhere; to avoid confusion with INT, annotators may club OAL with INT when appropriate but should mark OAL for generic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Clarity (CLA)
rubrics_metrics.description: CLA (Clarity) — reviewer comments about the clarity of writing, explanations, or compositional clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sentiment (POS/NEG/NEU) for CLA; reviewers comment on clarity often with Methodology and Overall sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Appropriateness (APR)
rubrics_metrics.description: APR (Appropriateness) — whether the submission is suitable for the venue/scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriateness is typically expressed at the Overall paper level; presence is low for top-tier venues where submissions are usually in-scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Novelty (NOV)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOV (Novelty) — comments assessing the newness or originality of the contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty often relates to Methodology, Problem Definition, and Related Work; explicit mentions of novelty are less frequent and sometimes implicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Substance (SUB)
rubrics_metrics.description: SUB (Substance) — the volume or substantive contribution of the work (e.g., sufficient experiments, theoretical depth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance connects to Methodology, Experiments, and Analysis; deficits in SUB often lead to criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Impact (IMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMP (Impact) — expected influence or significance of the work on the community or future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact comments often focus on Methodology, Related Work, and Results; reviewers may discuss future impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Meaningful Comparisons (CMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMP (Meaningful Comparisons) — adequacy of comparisons to prior methods and baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMP mostly relates to Related Work, Methodology, Experiments, and Results; bibliography co-occurs with CMP when citing prior works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Presentation & Formatting (PNF)
rubrics_metrics.description: PNF (Presentation and Formatting) — comments about write-up quality, formatting, tables/figures presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PNF issues are often minor comments and occur on Tables/Figures and Methodology; annotate when explicitly about presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Recommendation (REC)
rubrics_metrics.description: REC (Recommendation) — reviewer indicates overall recommendation for acceptance/rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers more often record recommendation in the form field than in text; when present in text, it usually pertains to the entire paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 — Aspect: Empirical/Theoretical Soundness (EMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: EMP (Empirical/Theoretical Soundness) — validity and rigor of empirical evaluation or theoretical claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMP is highly judged against Methodology, Experiments, Results, Related Work, Problem Definition, Data, and Analysis; a central aspect for ML venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Summary (SMY)
rubrics_metrics.description: SMY (Summary) — reviewer provides a brief summary of the paper reflecting understanding, usually at the review start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ideal review begins with a concise summary; mark SMY where the reviewer summarizes contribution/context. Summaries often accompany Methodology and Problem Definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Suggestion (SUG)
rubrics_metrics.description: SUG (Suggestion) — provides suggestions to the author to improve or include additional details for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: request for additional evidence, experiments, or artifacts. Suggestive comments are comparatively more common in accepted paper reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Deficit (DFT)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFT (Deficit) — highlights major/minor flaws or shortcomings in the paper; usually stated confidently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficit often overlaps with Criticism; mark when the reviewer explicitly points out shortcomings (e.g., missing explanations of core algorithms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Appreciation (APC)
rubrics_metrics.description: APC (Appreciation) — applauds the author, highlighting positive aspects or strengths of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciation is more prevalent in accepted-paper reviews and co-occurs with discussions of impact and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Discussion (DIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: DIS (Discussion) — neutral explanatory statements where the reviewer engages in explanation or additional insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion statements are usually neutral in polarity and help contextualize evaluation; often appear in Methodology, Related Work, Experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Question (QSN)
rubrics_metrics.description: QSN (Question) — reviewer explicitly poses a question to the authors (usually ends with a question mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions may ask for clarifications or highlight deficits; mark QSN when explicit interrogative forms are used. HCF features (presence of ?) strongly predict QSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Criticism (CRT)
rubrics_metrics.description: CRT (Criticism) — reviewer is critical of the work, highlighting deficits with explicit negative sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism often maps to Methodology, Experiments, and Results; presence higher in rejected paper reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3 — Purpose: Feedback (FBK)
rubrics_metrics.description: FBK (Feedback) — reviewer explicitly states their view toward the work, often leading to acceptance/rejection statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback statements are relatively rare in-text because recommendation fields are used; mark FBK when reviewer expresses an explicit stance (e.g., 'In overall, this paper is an accept').

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 4 — Significance: Major Comment (MAJ)
rubrics_metrics.description: MAJ (Major Comment) — strong statements highlighting opinionated views on major aspects or the entire paper; could indicate critical flaws or major appreciations that should influence meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/area chairs should consider MAJ comments in final decision-making and meta-review drafting. Major comments often highlight Criticism or Appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 4 — Significance: Minor Comment (MIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: MIN (Minor Comment) — comments not decisive for acceptance/rejection, typically on presentation, missing references, or small fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor comments can be quickly addressed by authors; many are about formatting or polishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 4 — Significance: General Comment (GEN)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN (General Comment) — regular comments that do not fall into Major or Minor categories; usually non-opinionated discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General comments often constitute summaries or neutral discussions within reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation guideline — sentence-wise annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform sentence-wise annotation for each review document for both the layers, but annotators may select text-segments; phrase-level annotation allowed when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sentence context when a single sentence is unclear. Make phrase-level annotation if a sentence addresses multiple aspects with varying sentiment. Put confusing instances in CANNOT DECIDE. Record sentiment (POS/NEG/NEU) for each label in Layer 1 and Layer 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation guideline — multi-label and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow multi-label annotations if multiple aspects or sections appear in the selected text-segment; use surrounding context for interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The task is multi-label: a review sentence can correspond to multiple sections/aspects/purposes. Annotators should read the entire review first to understand context and attitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation guideline — annotator qualifications & training
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotators should have relevant technical background and be trained: authors used two Master/PhD students and one bachelor hired full-time; they underwent a two-month exercise and ongoing meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct rigorous training on peer review process, ML paper formats, subjectivity, and labels. Resolve confusion cases in team meetings and maintain annotation interfaces that allow selecting text segments and checkboxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data procurement & preprocessing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use openreview.net API to crawl official reviews and associated metadata; store review text files with a naming convention (e.g., ICLR2018-Byxc4defh-R3.txt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprocessing performed: stop-word removal, stemming, removing irrelevant characters (whitespace, newlines, underscores), upper to lower-case conversion, and lemmatization. Provide full review and corresponding paper to annotators during labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-annotator agreement target & reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure multi-label inter-annotator agreement using Krippendorff's Alpha for each layer; reported values: Layer1=0.86, Layer2=0.70, Layer3=0.73, Layer4=0.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a subset of full reviews for IAA calculation and expand inter-annotation range to improve representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 1 definition — Review-paper section correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a peer review text, identify which paper section(s) (Layer 1 labels) the text corresponds to. This is a multi-label classification problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentence-level sequential classification; context (previous/next sentences) is important. Report micro-averaged F1 per label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 2 definition — Aspect-category detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a peer review text, identify which aspect(s) of the paper (Layer 2 labels) the reviewer is commenting on. Multi-label classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An allied task is aspect-specific sentiment detection. Evaluate with micro-averaged F1 scores per aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 3 definition — Review-statement purpose detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a review statement, identify its purpose/role (Layer 3 labels: Summary, Suggestion, Deficit, Appreciation, Discussion, Question, Criticism, Feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps capture reviewer intent; treat as sentence (or selected text-segment) classification with context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 4 definition — Review-statement significance detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a review statement, identify its significance level (Layer 4 labels: Major, Minor, General).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps surface crucial comments for meta-reviews; treat as sentence classification and report micro-averaged F1/accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 5 definition — Peer review summarization / meta-review generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate a concise summary of a review (or combined reviews) that highlights crucial aspects and could assist area chairs in drafting meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-review generation should include: a concise description of the submission's main content, a concise summary of reviewer discussion, and an explicit recommendation and justification. Evaluate extractive and abstractive models using ROUGE metrics; expect meta-review generation to be challenging because meta-reviews are opinionated beyond pure summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline representations & model recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended baseline feature representations: TF-IDF, TF-IDF with context, Universal Sentence Encoder (USE), Hand-Crafted Features (HCF), BERT-based Sequential Sentence Classification (BERT-SSC), and BERT+Transformer+CRF for sequence labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sequential sentence classification for Tasks 1-4. BERT-based baselines (SciBERT weights) outperform others; include surrounding sentence context for better performance. For classical models, Random Forest performed best among tested classifiers; SVM used for some tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-crafted features (HCF) — feature list
rubrics_metrics.description: A curated set of textual features for classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested features: # of nouns, # of adjectives, presence of exclamation sign, presence of numeric values, presence of %, presence of date, # of mathematical terms, # of adverbs, sentence length, # of verbs, # of label-specific frequent terms (dictionary), presence of wh-question words, presence of interrogation character. These features help, e.g., QSN is detected well due to '?'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training / evaluation protocol guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended experimental protocol: use an 80%:20% train-test split; report label-wise micro-averaged F1 scores and overall accuracies for Tasks 1–4. Use random oversampling to address class imbalance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate multiple classifiers (SVM, Naive Bayes, Decision Trees, SGD, Random Forest) and BERT variants. Report per-label F1 and overall task accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric guidance for classification and summarization
rubrics_metrics.description: For Tasks 1–4 (classification), report micro-averaged F1 scores per label and overall accuracy. For Task 5 (summarization), use ROUGE (R1, R2, R-L) precision/recall/F1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide label-wise F1 tables; for summarization, compare extractive (TextRank) and abstractive (Transformer) baselines and report ROUGE metrics separately for per-review and meta-review tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling notes — sequential context matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual dependencies between consecutive sentences are important for correct labeling; use sequential models that incorporate previous/next sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BERT-SSC and BERT+Transformer+CRF variants that exploit context outperform non-contextual baselines. For TF-IDF baselines, concatenate preceding and following sentences as context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing / naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Store crawled official reviews with a consistent filename scheme to map reviews to papers and review indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example used: ICLR2018-Byxc4defh-R3.txt denotes the third official review of paper id Byxc4defh from ICLR2018. Also store annotated versions separately (e.g., ICLR2018-Byxc4defh-R3-annotated.txt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: ambiguity handling & CANNOT DECIDE
rubrics_metrics.description: When annotators cannot confidently assign labels due to ambiguity, mark the instance as CANNOT DECIDE for later adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confusing instances are resolved in team meetings; ambiguous instances may be left out of the annotation process if consensus cannot be reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation about merging labels / future improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Merging overlapping section labels (e.g., INT and OAL) may resolve annotator ambiguity; more annotated data and improved label-specific features can improve low-resource labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors intend to merge some section labels and expand annotation to increase IAA and model performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews should not be simple summaries: they should include chair's opinionated view after reading reviews and must synthesize acceptance justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-review generation requires summarization, redundancy elimination, diversity estimation, and sentiment analysis in NLG settings. Reference: ICLR Metareview Guide.
